easy.def: To grow bigger or more serious.
examples: The argument escalated.
Prices escalate.
The storm escalated.

more.def: To grow quickly bigger or more serious.
examples: The small argument escalated into a big fight.
Prices escalate when many people want the same toy.
The wind escalated into a storm.
The hamster tried to escape from its cage.
The bird escaped out the window.
We escaped from the rain.

more.def: To get free from a place or from danger.
examples: The fish escaped through a hole in the net.
The people escaped the burning building through the back door.
Hot air escapes when you leave the door open.

easy.def: To go with someone to protect or guide them.
examples: The guard escorted us.
I escort my little sister.
The police escorted the parade.

more.def: To go with someone to guide them or keep them safe.
examples: The guard escorted us to our seats.
I escorted my little sister home.
Police cars escorted the parade.
I like dogs, especially puppies.
It is cold, especially at night.
I love fruit, especially grapes.

more.def: In a special way, or more than anything else.
examples: I love pets, especially cats.
It gets very cold here, especially at night.
She likes all sports, especially soccer.

easy.def: A short piece of writing about one subject.
examples: I wrote an essay.
The essay is about dogs.
The essay has five paragraphs.

more.def: A short piece of writing in which you give your ideas about a subject.
examples: I wrote an essay about my pet dog.
The essay had five paragraphs.
The teacher graded our essays.
Water is essential.
Sleep is essential.
A map is essential.
Water is essential for life.
A good map is essential for hiking.
Sleep is essential for growing kids.
They established a school.
The settlers established a town.
We will establish a club.

more.def: To set up something such as a school or a rule so that it will last.
examples: The settlers established a new town.
The students established a club for chess.
They established the school in 1900.

easy.def: A shop, restaurant or other place of business.
examples: The restaurant is a nice establishment.
That establishment is closed.
The establishment sells books.

more.def: A place where a business is carried on, such as a shop or a hotel.
examples: The restaurant is a family-owned establishment that has been open for fifty years.
The hotel is a very nice establishment near the lake.
This establishment sells fresh bread and pies.
The establishment of the school took ten years.
The establishment of the club was fun.
The town celebrated the establishment of a new library.

more.def: The act of setting something up or starting it.
examples: The establishment of our town's first school took place in 1850.
The class voted on the establishment of a new club.
The establishment of a new park gave the town more green space.

easy.def: A large piece of land with a big house.
examples: The family lives on a large estate.
The estate has a pond.
The estate has gardens.

more.def: A large piece of land with a big house, such as a farm or park owned by one family.
examples: The estate had gardens and a lake.
The rich family lived on a large estate in the country.
Peacocks walked around the estate.

easy.def: Respect and a good opinion of someone.
examples: I hold her in high esteem.
Self-esteem is feeling good about yourself.
He has our esteem.

more.def: Great respect and admiration for someone, or a good opinion of yourself.
examples: The whole town held the old teacher in high esteem.
Praise from her coach raised her self-esteem.
He earned the esteem of his classmates by being fair.
I estimate ten.
She estimated the weight.
Estimate the time.

more.def: To make a careful guess about the size or amount of something.
examples: I estimated the jar had a hundred beans.
She estimated the trip would take an hour.
The teacher asked us to estimate the length.
My estimate is twenty.
The estimate was close.
He made an estimate.

more.def: A careful guess about the size, amount or cost of something.
examples: My estimate is twenty minutes.
The estimate for the repairs was low.
His estimate was close to the real number.
